title: Knowledge Graphs as External Memory for LLM-based Scientific Assistants
abstract: Scientific assistants must remember the questions, observations, parameters, and intermediate results that accumulate across days or weeks of inquiry, and trace each conclusion back to its evidence. Large Language Models (LLMs) lack such a structured, persistent memory, which causes contextual degradation, hallucinations, and excessive cost from overusing the context window. This thesis proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that couples an LLM-based agent with a knowledge graph (KG) built on standardized formal languages (RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL, SHACL, SPARQL) and reusing existing ontologies (e.g. PROV-O) whenever possible. In contrast to state-of-the-art memory systems, which rely on schemaless or proprietary property graphs, our hypothesis is that grounding agent memory in open standards improves the six memory operations (consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting, retrieval, compression) through formal reasoning and declarative validation, at a latency overhead that stays negligible relative to the LLM call. We present the problem, three research questions and their hypotheses, a first experimental prototype that implements an end-to-end store-and-retrieve pipeline, and an evaluation plan combining the LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks with a test case in metabolomics.
journal: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)

title: EDA-Agent: A Multi-Agent AI System for RTL Verification, Circuit Debugging, and Semiconductor Design Automation -TCAD-2026-2322 (IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems)
abstract: Hardware verification and debugging traditionally consume over 70% of digital Integrated Circuit (IC) design cycles. Engineers spend thousands of hours manually parsing static timing reports, inspecting Value Change Dump (VCD) waveform traces, and writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA). EDA-Agent is an open-source, multi-agent AI platform designed to automate Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code analysis, functional testbench generation, waveform failure debugging, synthesis area estimation, and timing slack optimization. To overcome the hallucination risks of pure neural generation, EDA-Agent employs a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with strict deterministic boundaries: AST Static Analysis: A custom regex/AST parser deterministically evaluates design violations, such as latch inference conditions and blocking assignment race hazards. Trace-Based VCD Waveform Debugging: The system parses standard IEEE 1364 VCD files to build a temporal transition matrix, allowing the agent to back-track state transitions and map assertion failures directly to faulty source code lines. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): The system grounds its reasoning in an indexed database of IEEE 1800-2017 SystemVerilog standards, Yosys manuals, and OpenSTA documentation. Empirical evaluations of EDA-Agent demonstrate 100% unit test accuracy on core parsing components, 94.2% waveform-based bug localization accuracy, and a 37.5x acceleration in SystemVerilog testbench generation compared to manual human workflows.

title: Optimization-Driven Individual–Collective Intelligence: A Unified Framework for Adaptive Organization, Collaboration, and Iterative Optimization in Large Language Model Systems
abstract: Large language model (LLM) systems increasingly employ multiple agents to solve complex problems through cooperation, competition, role specialization, and iterative refinement. However, individual reasoning, collective organization, and swarm-based optimization are often modeled as separate mechanisms or combined through predefined workflows. This paper proposes an optimization-driven individual–collective intelligence framework that reverses the conventional conceptual progression from individual intelligence to collective intelligence and then to optimization. In the proposed framework, optimization objectives and performance feedback guide collective organization, collective organization regulates individual execution, and individual outcomes update subsequent optimization decisions. The framework comprises three interdependent layers: swarm-based optimization, collective intelligence, and individual intelligence. A feedback controller jointly considers solution quality, uncertainty, disagreement, diversity, computational expenditure, communication overhead, and task latency when determining search directions, agent participation, interaction structures, and execution strategies. A formal optimization objective is introduced to balance task performance and operational costs, while an adaptive collaboration policy determines when independent execution, cooperative reasoning, cross-verification, or further optimization is appropriate. The framework also specifies a reference algorithm, testable research hypotheses, evaluation metrics, baseline systems, and an experimental protocol. Unlike approaches that optimize only model configurations or fixed multi-agent workflows, the proposed framework treats optimization policy, collective organization, and individual execution as mutually dependent components of a closed-loop system. The framework is a research proposal rather than an empirically validated method. Its contribution must therefore be established through controlled experiments comparing adaptive and fixed-organization alternatives across reasoning, optimization, and coordination tasks.

title: SCOPE: Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction for Robot Long-term Planning Datasets
abstract: Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) stands as a fundamental challenge in robotics, essential for enabling autonomous agents to execute complex, long-horizon tasks in diverse environments. While Large Language Models (LLMs) introduce a new paradigm for TAMP by leveraging extensive common sense, their inherent reasoning limitations hinder direct application, and fine-tuning strategies to enhance these capabilities are currently bottlenecked by the scarcity of high-quality datasets. Existing automated generation methods often suffer from homogeneity, limiting model generalization, and unsolvability, where hallucinated scene graphs create physical mismatches with task goals. To address these issues, we propose Scene-graph Construction Optimized by Plan Error-correction (SCOPE), an automated framework designed to generate diverse and executable TAMP datasets. SCOPE incorporates multi-level diversity metrics to maximize the information entropy of scenarios. Crucially, it introduces a Plan Feedback Error-correction pipeline that utilizes planner execution failures as feedback signals to retroactively rectify logical inconsistencies in scene graphs, ensuring physical feasibility. Experimental results demonstrate that SCOPE exhibits greater robustness to erroneous scene graphs and generates higher-quality data. When utilized for LLM fine-tuning, SCOPE-generated data yield a downstream TAMP model that achieves an absolute 12.33% gain in success rate over its counterpart fine-tuned with data generated by DELTA, a state-of-the-art PDDL-based planner.

title: Spark-Audio 1.0 Technical Report
abstract: This paper introduces Spark-Audio 1.0, a speech foundation model trained on domestically produced computing infrastructure. The model accepts text and speech inputs and generates text outputs. It supports multilingual (99 languages) and multi-dialect (202 dialects) speech recognition, speech translation, audio perception and understanding, and both text- and speech-based dialogue, marking a shift from merely ``hearing clearly'' to genuinely ``understanding'' speech. Architecturally, Spark-Audio 1.0 couples a 0.65B-parameter dense audio encoder with a 30B-A3B Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language model (LLM). The audio encoder is pretrained with representation-enhanced BEST-RQ and then refined through multi-task supervised training. The audio--LLM is trained through staged pretraining, followed by post-training that combines supervised fine-tuning with on-policy distillation. In total, the model is trained on 13 million hours of audio data together with large-scale text data. We evaluate Spark-Audio 1.0 on mainstream audio and text benchmarks, as well as on in-house test sets drawn from real-world application scenarios. Despite using substantially less audio training data than Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, Spark-Audio 1.0 achieves comparable performance on most audio and text tasks, outperforms it in multilingual speech recognition, spoken dialogue, and real-world application scenarios, and approaches the performance of larger closed-source models. Nevertheless, there remains room for improvement in instruction following and complex audio reasoning. Finally, the successful training of Spark-Audio 1.0 on domestic hardware, including Huawei Ascend 910B and Hygon BW1000 chips, demonstrates the feasibility of a domestic technical pathway for building speech foundation models.

title: LLM Roulette-Wheel Intelligence: Adaptive Probabilistic Selection and Evolution of Model Coordination Strategies
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit heterogeneous capabilities, costs, response latencies, and reliability across tasks. Existing model-routing and multi-agent coordination approaches address parts of this problem, but a general framework for probabilistically allocating both model execution and coordination strategies according to task conditions and observed outcomes remains an important research direction. This paper proposes LLM Roulette-Wheel Intelligence (LLM-RWI), a feedback-driven framework that adapts the classical roulette-wheel selection principle to the organization of LLM-based intelligent systems. Rather than selecting models solely through fixed rankings or deterministic routing, LLM-RWI assigns probabilities to a joint action space containing candidate models, independent execution, self-correction, cross-model verification, and collaborative reasoning. These probabilities depend on task context, estimated utility, uncertainty, computational cost, latency, and historical feedback. After execution, the system updates its estimates using observed quality and resource consumption, thereby adapting subsequent selection decisions. The framework also incorporates exploration control, diversity preservation, budget constraints, and an adaptive stopping criterion. A formal objective is developed to characterize the trade-offs among answer quality, resource expenditure, latency, and coordination overhead. The paper presents the algorithm, analytical properties under explicit assumptions, and a reproducible experimental protocol for comparing the proposed approach with random selection, fixed roulette-wheel selection, adaptive model routing, contextual bandits, and existing multi-agent coordination methods. The framework is presented as a research proposal; its empirical superiority and the novelty of its complete formulation require experimental validation and systematic comparison with prior work.

title: PIU Smart Intelligence Agents: Design and Implementation of a Security-Aware Multi-Agent Architecture for Enterprise Intelligence
abstract: Enterprises increasingly rely on heterogeneous documents, relational databases, and analytical systems to support information retrieval and business decision-making. Integrating large language models (LLMs) with these sources introduces challenges in evidence reliability, analytical correctness, access control, and operational resilience. This paper presents PIU Smart Intelligence Agents, a security-aware multi-agent architecture designed to integrate enterprise document intelligence, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), semantic search, document summarization, naturallanguage-to-SQL analytics, key performance indicator (KPI) generation, and conversational AI within a common application and governance framework. The proposed architecture organizes specialized AI capabilities around shared services for authentication, authorization, request validation, provider integration, observability, and controlled data access. Its document-processing workflow encompasses file validation, text extraction, optical character recognition for scanned documents, normalization, chunking, embedding generation, and vector-based indexing. The structured-analytics workflow separates schema-aware query generation from SQL validation, restricted database execution, and result interpretation. The architecture also addresses provider compatibility, timeout handling, failure recovery, document lifecycle management, and traceability of generated outputs. The source implementation reports 1,242 automated tests passed and two integration tests skipped. These results are reported implementation evidence and have not been independently reproduced. The available evidence does not establish comprehensive external RAG benchmark performance, quantitative correctness across all agents, independently validated security effectiveness, or production-scale performance and recovery guarantees. Accordingly, this study presents an integrated engineering architecture and identifies a reproducible evaluation framework for assessing its effectiveness. The principal contribution is the systematic integration of heterogeneous enterprise AI capabilities with explicit governance and validation requirements, rather than the introduction of a new learning or retrieval algorithm. Future work should prioritize agent-specific correctness testing, retrieval and answer-quality benchmarks, adversarial security evaluation, controlled load testing, and recovery verification.
journal: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

title: Future of AI in English Language Education: Trends and Predictions
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming English language education (ELE) by enabling personalized learning, automated assessment, adaptive content generation, and immersive practice environments. This paper synthesizes current developments, identifies emergent trends, and offers evidence-informed predictions about how AI will shape classroom practice, curriculum design, assessment, teacher roles, and policy over the next decade. Drawing on interdisciplinary literature from computer-assisted language learning (CALL), intelligent tutoring systems (ITS), natural language processing (NLP), and educational policy, the paper argues that the most significant near-term impact will stem from hybrid systems that combine large language models (LLMs) with pedagogically informed scaffolding and teacher mediation. Key trends discussed include (1) ubiquitous personalized feedback and adaptive pathways; (2) automated, formative assessment with rich analytics; (3) realistic speaking/listening practice via multimodal conversational agents and immersive virtual environments; (4) AI-assisted material creation and differentiation for diverse learner needs; and (5) data-driven teacher support and professional development. Predictions address likely improvements in scalability and access, as well as persistent challenges: bias and fairness in language models, privacy and data governance, over-reliance on automated feedback, and the need for robust teacher training and curricular alignment. The paper concludes with practical recommendations for educators, institutions, and policymakers to harness AI’s affordances while safeguarding equity, transparency, and pedagogical quality. These include adopting hybrid human–AI workflows, emphasizing explainability and interpretability in tools, developing clear data-ethics policies, investing in teacher capacity building, and prioritizing research-practice partnerships. The analysis aims to be actionable for practitioners and decision-makers planning for an AI-augmented future of English language learning. Keywords: artificial intelligence, English language education, adaptive learning, large language models, assessment, teacher role, ethics

title: A Hybrid Ranking–LLM Pipeline for Statement‑Level Fault Localization
abstract: (A) Background: This work provide a novel statement-level fault localization technique that combines Large Language Model (LLM) with statistical, evolution and test-coverage features on a five-stage pipeline. Notably, we employ five algorithms for performance comparison. We also investigate the propagation of faults from a framework to its downstream dependency applications (100 applications) in Machine Learning (ML) and non-ML domain across Java and Python programming language. We are motivated to carry out this study because of the ever-growing integration of LLM into modern software application so that quality of such application is kept up-to-date optimally from the angle of fault localization and fault propagation. Next, we evaluate our approach on existing baseline fault localization techniques on baseline datasets (Defects4J and Tests4Py) in which our result outperforms the best existing techniques on the baselines. Furthermore, we evaluate our approach with stand-alone Claude reasoning model on baseline datasets (Defects4J and Tests4Py) and we found that the Top-1 prediction of our approach outperforms Claude's Top-1 prediction. Hence, we justify our study applicability to real-world scenarios. We provide the step-wise approach of our implementation below. (B) Prerequisite Install all the tool version in the requirements.txt located at the root directoryCreate a GitHub API key to be able to use our data extraction scriptCreate a Groq OpenAPI key to be able to use free-tier version of Qwen 3.8-27BCreate a Claude Anthropic key on Claude official platform to be able to use the Claude evaluation script and fund your Claude account with minimum of $500 (based on number of faults to be analyzed) (C) Dataset Create a folder in the root directory named "all_json", where all extracted and processed dataset in our pipeline are located. Extract the zip file "all_json_java" and "all_json_python" into the "all_json" folder The folder "outputs" is automatically created in the path "all_json/outputs" w hen you run any of the analysis script, which is used as location for all generated visual outputs of ur entire pipeline. (D) Scripts run phase1.py to extra the raw JSON dataset of the 280 frameworks that we considered run phase2.py to extra the JSON dataset of the dependent applications run phase3.py to convert all the dependency applications to statement level to train the ranking algorithms run phase4.py to train the five algorithms on the training set from phase3.py run phase5.py to evaluate the five algorithms against existing baselines on Defects4J and Tests4Py benchmark run claude_evaluation_on_benchmarks.py to evaluate on the Top-1 prediction of Claude as a standalone fault localizer against our model on Defects4J and Tests4Py benchmark run analysis_phase1, analysis_phase2, analysis_phase3, analysis_phase4 to statistically analyze the corresponding results in Phases1-4 (E) Note Some analysis results are printed on the console when you run the script, while all visualization plots are saved in the "all_json/outputs" directory You require minimum of 2TB available disc space and 32Gb memory to run our architecture because of the large amount of dataset involved in this study If you run on windows operating system, you are require to setup Windows Subsystem for Linux environment to be able to extract dataset for Defectst4J and Tests4Py

title: ReflectPO: Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
abstract: With external tools, large language models (LLMs) can tackle complex tasks through sustained environmental interaction. LLM-based agents are therefore increasingly used to tackle complex long-horizon tasks in real-world environments. However, these tasks involve sequential, interdependent decisions and changes in environmental states. Early execution errors affect subsequent interaction histories and environmental states, and their effects accumulate along the decision chain. To address this challenge, we propose Reflection-Guided Policy Optimization (ReflectPO), a reinforcement learning framework for autonomous error recovery in long-horizon tasks. ReflectPO comprises two core components. The first is Reflection-Guided Sampling. We use branch differences and repeated visits in interaction trajectories to construct hints for error recovery. The second is Tree-Structured Credit Assignment. We organize sampled trajectories into trees and assign action-level credit using parent--child reward differences and recovery gains. Experiments over two long-horizon tool-use benchmarks show that ReflectPO outperforms multiple existing baselines in most domains. It also achieves the best overall performance on average. Further analyses show that ReflectPO effectively improves agents' ability to recognize their own deviations, recover from erroneous states, and continue making progress toward task completion.

title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems Are Vulnerable to Herding and Runaway Cascades
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate in multi-agent systems where they collaborate by responding to others' choices, creating endogenous feedback loops with vulnerability to social influence, herding behavior and runaway cascades. Following the design of the classic Music Lab experiment, we tested this vulnerability in large populations of LLM agents that recommended unfamiliar songs, with or without exposure to cumulative recommendation counts. Exposure led to runaway cascades that generated extreme and unpredictable collective recommendations increasingly divergent from a song's intrinsic appeal. Compared to humans, LLM populations were generally far more susceptible to herding behavior, and unlike humans, LLM cascades were less able to self-correct. This vulnerability has implications for multi-agent collaboration in recommender systems, automated evaluation, complex problem-solving, and unauthorized conspiracies.

title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
abstract: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.
